claims.claim_text: Case Number: SC-009
Date of Incident: March 11, 2021
Time of Incident: Approximately 1818 hours to 1839 hours
Location: Pacific Coast Highway, Laguna Beach, CA
Reporting Officer: Officer D. Kessler
Badge Number: 3891
Subject: Tyler Brandt, Male, approximately 30 years old, White, black sweatshirt, light blue t-shirt underneath
Officer(s): Officer D. Kessler, Corporal A. Novak (PIT maneuver), Officer M. Trujillo, Sergeant R. Holt
Witness(es): None at scene of shooting
On March 11, 2021, at approximately 1818 hours, I was driving southbound on Pacific Coast Highway in my marked Laguna Beach Police Department patrol vehicle
I observed a white Mercedes sedan traveling southbound at a high rate of speed
I attempted to pace the Mercedes and observed erratic driving behavior, including veering on and off the shoulder
I believed the driver was potentially impaired
I broadcast over the radio my intent to conduct a traffic stop and requested immediate backup at approximately 1819 hours
The driver of the Mercedes initially appeared to comply, pulling the vehicle onto the northbound shoulder of Pacific Coast Highway
I exited my patrol vehicle and began approaching the vehicle on the passenger side
As I reached the rear quarter panel of the Mercedes, the driver abruptly accelerated away from the traffic stop
The driver made a hard-right turn across oncoming traffic
A vehicle pursuit ensued
During the pursuit, the subject collided with two civilian vehicles, causing one vehicle to overturn
I continued the pursuit with emergency lights and sirens activated
Additional Laguna Beach Police units joined the pursuit
An Orange County Sheriff helicopter provided aerial support
The subject reached speeds of approximately 90 miles per hour
The subject was observed driving on the wrong side of the road and swerving into oncoming traffic
Laguna Beach Police officers successfully deployed a spike strip, which caused all four tires of the Mercedes to deflate
Despite the tire damage, the subject continued to flee
The subject continued driving on deflated tires for approximately two additional miles
Corporal Novak successfully executed a pursuit intervention technique (PIT) maneuver, bringing the Mercedes to a stop in the southbound lane of Pacific Coast Highway
The vehicle came to rest facing north
My patrol unit, Officer Trujillo's unit, and Sergeant Holt's unit took positions approximately 15 feet from the stopped Mercedes
All units had their takedown lights and spotlights illuminated and directed at the subject
I was positioned in the center, with Officer Trujillo to my left and Sergeant Holt to my right
Upon the vehicle coming to a stop, I observed the subject remain seated in the driver's seat for approximately 30 seconds, appearing to look around the interior of the vehicle
The subject then exited the vehicle and immediately turned to face the officers
The subject placed his left hand behind his back and made a distinct reaching motion toward his left hip area
I interpreted this movement as consistent with someone reaching for a concealed firearm
I commanded the subject to get on the ground
The subject did not comply and instead began advancing toward me and the other officers in a rapid, deliberate manner
The subject suddenly extended both arms forward at chest height with his hands together in a manner that simulated pointing a firearm directly at me
I discharged my department-issued Glock 17 firearm, firing four rounds at the subject at approximately 1839 hours
Despite being struck, the subject remained on his feet and continued advancing toward the officers
The subject yelled profanities at the officers while continuing to make threatening gestures consistent with pointing a weapon
Officer Trujillo deployed his department-issued Taser, which struck the subject and caused him to fall to the ground
Sergeant Holt broadcast over the radio that shots had been fired and a Taser had been deployed
I approached the subject with Officer Trujillo, and we placed the subject in handcuffs
We immediately began rendering first aid
I conducted a search of the subject's person and recovered a small black semi-automatic pistol from the subject's right front waistband area
Laguna Beach Fire Department paramedics arrived at approximately 1848 hours
and transported the subject to Mission Hospital in Mission Viejo, where he underwent surgery
The subject survived his injuries, which included two gunshot wounds to the upper torso and one to the left forearm
Body-worn camera footage (Officer Kessler, Officer Trujillo, Sergeant Holt)
Patrol vehicle video recordings
One (1) Black Taser X26 and one (1) black Taser cartridge
One (1) black sweatshirt
One (1) light blue t-shirt
One (1) blue RBX tennis shoe
Six (6) cartridge casings, 9mm
172 scene photographs
Subject transported to Mission Hospital Mission Viejo for emergency surgery
Subject survived
Criminal charges filed
Scene secured for OCDA investigation
Officer Signature: D. Kessler
Date of Report: March 11, 2021
